title: Two steady lakes, one bad year
hook: Both lakes have given 120 fish a year for years. Then a disease hits both.

knows: a lake adds at most 125 fish a year, at 500 fish (steady-catch-from-a-lake)
doesNotKnow: that a fixed quota below the lake's best growth has a second balance point (400 fish here) below which the lake drains, and that a fixed share has none

misconception: A catch that has been steady for years is safe. A fixed number is the cautious rule: it never takes more than it says.
objective: The learner can explain why a fixed catch of 120 empties a lake knocked down to 300 (growth 105 is below the catch) while a 20% share recovers (its catch shrinks with the stock), and that the fixed number has a tipping point (400 here) the share lacks.

claims.text: In the model, after a disease kills half of each lake in year 10, lake A (120 a year) is empty in year 17 (t = 16.9) and lake B (20% a year) is back to 600 by year 60; after a 30% loss both recover (A 589, B 600 at year 60). Reveal: "After a 30% loss both lakes came back. After a 50% loss, lake B recovered to 600, but lake A was empty in year 17." Stage readout: "year 60: A empty · B 600 fish".
claims.source: simulate() in Demo.tsx: dN/dt = 0.5N(1 - N/1000) - H, H = 120 or 0.2N, N(0) = 600, disease multiplies N by 0.7 or 0.5 at year 10, Euler dt 0.001. Builder re-run 2026-10-14 (node strip-types): quota 30% end 588.57 (year 20: 446); share 30% 600.00 (587); quota 50% empty at t = 16.933; share 50% 600.00 (year 20: 572). Matches check script E2 (company/domains/briefs/checks/life-wave-j-check.mjs). 'Year 17' rounds 16.9 up, as in steady-catch-from-a-lake.
claims.note: Re-ran simulate() copied from Demo.tsx (node strip-types): quota 30% end 588.57 (year 20: 446.4); share 30% 600.00 (587.5); quota 50% empty at t = 16.933 -> yr() 17; share 50% 600.00 (571.6). Stage readouts: 'year 60: A 589 fish · B 600 fish' (30%), 'year 60: A empty · B 600 fish' (50%), and 'A 600 · B 600' with no disease. Matches check script E2 (re-run): quota 0.5 empty at 16.9.

claims.text: With a fixed catch of 120, growth equals the catch at 400 and 600 fish; below 400 the catch exceeds growth (at 300 fish the lake adds only 105 a year), so the lake drains. Reveal: "Lake A's catch stays 120 however few fish remain. At 300 fish the lake adds only 105 a year, so each year takes more than it adds." Stage: "at 300 fish: grows 105, A takes 120" and the dashed line "A's tipping point: 400".
claims.source: Solve 0.5N(1 - N/1000) = 120: N^2 - 1000N + 240000 = 0, N = 400 or 600. Growth at 300: 0.5 x 300 x 0.7 = 105 < 120. Below 400 growth is below 120, so dN/dt < 0 and N falls to 0.
claims.note: Derivation: 0.5N(1 - N/1000) = 120 gives N = 400 or 600; growthAt(300) = 105 exactly as rendered; growth < 120 at every integer N in 1-399 (node). The 30% case dips to 420 > 400 and recovers, consistent with the tipping point.

claims.text: With a fixed 20% catch, growth exceeds the catch at every stock below 600, so the lake returns to 600 from any positive stock; at 300 fish the 20% catch is 60. Reveal: "Lake B's 20% shrinks with the stock: 60 fish at 300. A fixed number has a tipping point, 400 fish here; a fixed share has none."
claims.source: 0.5N(1 - N/1000) > 0.2N  <=>  0.5(1 - N/1000) > 0.2  <=>  N < 600, for N > 0. 0.2 x 300 = 60. The quota's lower balance point is 400 (claim 2); the share rule has only N = 0 and N = 600 as balance points, and 0 is unstable.
claims.note: Derivation: 0.5N(1 - N/1000) > 0.2N iff N < 600 (checked at every integer N in 1-599); 0.2 x 300 = 60. The share rule's balance points are 0 (unstable) and 600.

claims.text: Toy model: fixed growth rate and limit, one disease, no chance or age structure; not fishing advice. Stage: "Toy lakes: fish add 0.5·N·(1 − N/1000) a year. A takes 120 a year; B takes 20%." Reveal: "Toy model, not fishing advice."
claims.source: The lesson's model (brief bad-year-breaks-the-quota, company/domains/briefs/life.ecology-body.md #2). The brief's optional real-world context (constant-catch vs constant-effort rules, Hilborn and Walters 1992) is not on the card.
claims.note: Convention: the stage and the reveal describe the model accurately (growth 0.5N(1 - N/1000), catch 120 or 20%, one disease) and disclaim fishing advice. No literature sentence is on the card.

claims.text: Setup on the locked stage: two lakes of 600 fish, steady for years; lake A catches 120 fish a year, lake B catches 20% a year, also 120 now.
claims.source: Both rules are at a balance point at 600: growth 0.5 x 600 x 0.4 = 120 = quota = 0.2 x 600.
claims.note: Derivation: growth at 600 = 0.5 x 600 x 0.4 = 120 = quota = 0.2 x 600; both kill-0 runs stay at 600.

recall.question: Two fisheries both take 1,000 tonnes a year from a stock that has been steady for decades. One takes a fixed 1,000 tonnes; the other takes a fixed share. A bad year halves the stock. Which is more at risk?
options: Both the same: they took the same catch
recall.why: A fixed number keeps taking the same amount when the stock is small and grows slowly, so it can take more than the stock adds and drain it. A fixed share shrinks with the stock.
